raw_response:
I will keep the full 3.0 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is what my land, water, and labor are already set up for. I do not start from zero each year; I start from what has held yield before and then adjust a little for cost and field condition. With only 3 mu, every bag of fertilizer matters, but yield matters more, so I will not cut fertilizer too hard. I have well irrigation, so I can support wheat at key stages and give maize water when it is setting yield. For wheat, I will use an improved variety and keep fertilizer a bit heavier on nitrogen, because wheat on our side responds clearly when base fertilizer is adequate and the topdressing is not delayed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen strong, and make sure phosphorus and potassium are not empty, because if maize stands weak after wheat stubble, it is hard to recover later. I will stay with rotary tillage because on a small plot it is practical, fast, and fits my family labor. I will spray when needed, but I will not save money by missing the main disease and insect windows, because losing yield costs more than one extra application.
